transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Sophie, Marcus (Redwood); Priya, Dan, Lina (Velox)

[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm sophie kim from redwood inference, i'll kick off real quick, marcus will do the technical walkthrough, today we'll focus on the sdk integration - python and typescript, auth, env setup and quickstarts, is that right priya?
[00:12] Priya: yea that's perfect thanks, our goal is to see how fast our eng team can get a POC up and measure latency/cost, and also check security controls - sso, kms, data residency.
[00:23] Marcus: great. quick agenda: install, auth, simple generate + streaming, embeddings, error handling and retry patterns, then brief on dedicated vs hosted and private options. i'll show a tiny python quickstart and a typescript snippet.
[00:40] Dan: one ask - we run in us-east and eu-west, need multi-region routing, and want to understand kv cache behavior with bursty traffic.
[00:50] Marcus: noted - we route by policy, and the runtime supports prefix/KV cache, sorry sometimes our transcriber says 'KV cash' but it's KV cache, small mishears.
[01:02] Marcus: ok first: pip install redwood-inference, set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. quick example - (paraphrased)
[01:12] Marcus: python snippet: from redwood import Client; c = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), region='us-east'); resp = c.generate(model='redwood-2-13b', prompt='Summarize...')
[01:25] Marcus: for streaming, you switch to stream=True and handle partial tokens, same pattern in TS with @redwood/inference. example: const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-east'}); const stream = client.generateStream(...).
[01:40] Priya: are there official quickstart repos? links?
[01:45] Sophie: yes, i'll drop the quickstart repo link in the followup email and also in the notes - quickstart includes python and typescript samples, dockerfile, and a sample benchmark script.
[01:55] Lina: about auth and keys - we need SSO + role-based access and KMS integration for private. Do you support customer-managed KMS?
[02:05] Marcus: yes - for private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption and can sign BAA/SLA clauses; we'll share SOC2 docs. sometimes the transcriber shows 'KMS HNMS' but it's KMS/HSM.
[02:20] Dan: any special network setup for private? vpc peering?
[02:25] Marcus: private has VPC and on-prem options - you can peering or use private link; we'll send topology doc. for dedicated vs hosted, think of dedicated as reserved capacity - predictable throughput and isolation. hosted is fastest to get started.
[02:40] Priya: latency numbers - can we expect 50-100ms per token?
[02:45] Marcus: depends on model size and batch config; in our benchmarks redwood-2-small is ~20-40ms tail p50 on A100 for short sequences, larger models are higher. we'll run a focused POC to measure your real workload.
[03:00] Marcus: SDK notes: environment variables, retry/backoff built-in, idempotency keys for batches, and token-level cost reporting via the console. example error handling: catch 429 and backoff, for long-tail latency use streaming timeouts.
[03:20] Sophie: on pricing - we have usage-based for hosted, reserved commit for dedicated; i'll send the dedicated worksheet.
[03:30] Dan: what about model fallbacks during capacity shortage?
[03:35] Marcus: we have smart routing - fallback to compatible variants (smaller quantized models) and ability to route by cost or latency policy. For POC we can pin a model version.
[03:50] Priya: data retention and audit logs?
[03:55] Marcus: there's audit logs and per-token tracing in console; retention configurable for dedicated/private. for hosted we have default retention policy, but enterprise contracts can change that.
[04:10] Priya: ok can you show the typescript quickstart?
[04:15] Marcus: sure, quick paste: // install yarn add @redwood/inference 
[04:20] Marcus: const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-east-1'}); await client.generate({model: 'redwood-2-small', prompt: '...'});
[04:32] Marcus: note: set REDWOOD_REGION to match your target region so we can route to nearest infra.
[04:40] Dan: for the benchmark script - will it do continuous streaming concurrency?
[04:45] Marcus: the sample benchmark uses a small harness that replays traces at adjustable QPS and measures p50/p95 tail; it also supports k8s based load agents if you want to run in your VPC.
[04:58] Lina: security review - we need SOC2, iso27001, and penetration test reports to move forward.
[05:05] Sophie: we'll attach those docs in the followup (SOC2 report, pen test summary) and include the contact for compliance.
[05:15] Priya: timeline - we want a 4 week POC to validate latency and cost, then decision. Is that reasonable?
[05:22] Marcus: yes, common. we'll propose a POC plan: week 0 setup + baseline, week 1 benchmarking, week 2 integration tests, week 3 review and results.
[05:34] Dan: who on your side runs the POC?
[05:37] Sophie: our solutions engineer (marcus) will be the lead, and i'll coordinate. we'll provide the POC checklist and runbooks.
[05:45] Marcus: quick gotcha: if you do on-prem the model weights and runtime setup are different - quantization and kernel selection matter, we'll document recommended quant profiles.
[05:58] Marcus: transcription note: sometimes 'redwood console' shows up as 'red wood console' in the notes, just ignore small spacing.
[06:08] Priya: ok last question - any client side best practices for tokenization costs? we have multi-turn chat flows.
[06:15] Marcus: yes: prefix caching, truncate context with heuristics, offload embeddings to cheap batches, and use reranking to avoid large generation. Optimize tool suggests config.
[06:30] Sophie: wrap up - recap next steps, i'll email pricing + SOC2 + quickstart repo + POC times. marcus will share sample benchmark and POC checklist. velox will share test S3 and request traces.
[06:45] Priya: thanks all, we'll confirm proposed kickoff time.
[06:50] Sophie: great thanks everyone, bye!

Notes: occasional transcription errors (KV cash, KMS HNMS, red wood). Shared artifacts: quickstart repo (link will be provided), dedicated capacity worksheet (will be sent), SOC2 and pen test docs (to be attached).
